hypothesis: single-pass GQA-grouped Triton baseline (grid (B,8), 4 shared qo-heads/program, tl.dot QK/PV, online base-2 softmax) hugely beats the Python double-loop reference and establishes a correct timing baseline
change_summary: grid (B,num_kv_heads); each program computes G=4 query heads sharing one kv head so each (token,kv) K/V slice is loaded once; QK via tl.dot bf16->fp32, PV via tl.dot(p.bf16, v.bf16)->fp32; base-2 online softmax with qk_scale=sm_scale*log2(e); lse=m+log2(l); empty/l==0 guard -> out=0, lse=-inf; BLOCK_N=64, num_warps=4, num_stages=2
decision_reason: correct on all 5 workloads; sets reference. Bottleneck workloads: W3 (99x, batch=1 launch/occupancy-bound) and W1 (416x, sol=227us vs ~43us HBM floor -> long-sequence latency, low CTA count=128). These motivate split-K/flash-decoding next.
